subtitle: Gulbadan Begum and the Memory of an Empire

panels.shot: slow three-quarter view, medium close-up, with architectural backdrop
panels.action: Gulbadan Begum sits dignified on a low cushion in a Mughal chamber, an open Persian manuscript before her, behind her the domes and red sandstone arcades of Fatehpur Sikri glow in the late light.

dialogue.text: In Akbar’s marble halls, one woman of Babur’s blood sharpened her reed pen and quietly set an empire’s memory to paper.

i18n.hi: अकबर के संगमरमर महलों में, बाबर की वंशज एक औरत ने सरक़ कलम तेज़ की और चुपचाप साम्राज्य की यादें काग़ज़ पर उतार दीं।

panels.shot: wide interior establishing shot, slightly high angle
panels.action: Older Gulbadan Begum, veiled yet unveiled of face, sits in a sunlit chamber of Fatehpur Sikri, shelves of manuscripts behind her, attendants distant and small, while she gazes through a jali screen toward the bustling imperial city.

dialogue.text: By the late 1580s, Fatehpur Sikri rang with arguments of scholars and the marching feet of soldiers, but in one quiet women’s apartment, a princess turned the past over in her hands like a string of beads.

i18n.hi: 1580 के आख़िर तक, फ़तेहपुर सीकरी में विद्वानों की बहस और सिपाहियों की चाल गूंजती थी, पर एक शांत ज़ेनाना कमरे में एक राजकुमारी अतीत को मनके की माला-सा उलट-पलट रही थी।

panels.shot: medium shot, low angle to give subtle prominence
panels.action: Gulbadan sits before a writing board, a reed pen poised above fresh paper; beside her, a neatly stacked pile of blank folios hints at the work ahead, while a young female scribe waits respectfully.

dialogue.text: Gulbadan Begum, daughter of Babur, half-sister of Humayun, aunt of Akbar, had seen Kabul’s mountain winds and the dust of Indian plains. Now, her nephew asked her to write of those days.

i18n.hi: बाबर की बेटी, हुमायूँ की सौतेली बहन, अकबर की फूफी — गुलबदन बेगम ने काबुल की पहाड़ी हवा और हिन्दुस्तान की धूल दोनों देखी थीं। अब उनका भतीजा उनसे उन दिनों को लिखने की दरख़्वास्त कर रहा था।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Gulbadan’s face, eyes distant
panels.action: Her lined yet steady face fills the frame, eyes half-closed as if seeing a far-off landscape, the light from a narrow window tracing the fine wrinkles of age and the firmness of her jaw.

dialogue.speaker: gulbadan_begum
dialogue.text: How many lives lie between my father’s tents and this stone city?

i18n.hi: मेरे बाप के ख़ेमों से इस पत्थर के शहर तक कितनी ज़िंदगियाँ बिछी हैं?

panels.shot: soft-edged memory tableau, wide landscape shot
panels.action: A younger Gulbadan, as a child, rides within a covered howdah of a small caravan crossing a rocky pass near Kabul, snow-dusted hills beyond, while hardy Mughal soldiers and women of the camp move alongside.

dialogue.text: Her earliest memories were not marble pavilions but the rough camps of Babur’s household, women and children moving with the army, their lives tied to a line of kings chasing fortune across Kabul and Hindustan.

i18n.hi: उसकी सबसे पहली यादें संगमरमर के महल नहीं, बाबर के उखड़े हुए डेरों की थीं—औरतें-बच्चे फ़ौज के साथ चलते, उनकी ज़िंदगी राजाओं की उस कड़ी से बंधी जो क़िस्मत के पीछे काबुल और हिन्दुस्तान में दौड़ती थी।

panels.shot: medium shot, interior memory of the haram, eye-level
panels.action: In an earlier Mughal haram in Agra, middle-aged Gulbadan stands among other royal women, their veils light and informal, as courtiers announce news of Humayun’s rise; she listens with attentive, serious eyes.

dialogue.text: As Humayun took Babur’s place, Gulbadan grew into one of the senior women of the dynasty, watching brothers, cousins and rivals move in and out of favour, alliance and exile.

i18n.hi: हुमायूँ ने बाबर की गद्दी सँभाली तो गुलबदन सल्तनत की बुज़ुर्ग बेगमों में गिनी जाने लगी—भाइयों, चचेरों और दुश्मनों को रुतबे, रिश्तों और जला-वतनियों में उठते-गिरते देखती रही।

panels.shot: wide shot of a courtyard, slightly elevated angle
panels.action: Within a Mughal palace courtyard some years earlier, Gulbadan stands with other women as news of Humayun’s defeat and flight is whispered about; their faces are controlled but tense, servants frozen mid-gesture.

dialogue.text: She saw the empire crumble under Humayun, heard of his hurried flights and uneasy shelters. For the women, defeat meant new journeys, uncertain loyalties, and the careful keeping of kin in dangerous times.

i18n.hi: उसने हुमायूँ के दौर में साम्राज्य को बिखरते देखा, उसकी हड़बड़ी भागों और बेचैन पनाहों की ख़बरें सुनीं। औरतों के लिए हार का मतलब था नए सफ़र, डगमग वफ़ादारियाँ और ख़तरे के दिनों में ख़ून के रिश्‍तों को सँभालकर रखना।

panels.shot: medium shot, dimly lit interior, candlelight
panels.action: In a darker Kabul chamber years later, Gulbadan sits near other senior women, a small boy who will be Akbar playing at their feet, while a messenger bows with tidings of Humayun’s restored throne and sudden death.

dialogue.text: She lived through the dizzy swing of fortune: Humayun’s return to power, his fall from the library steps in Delhi, the child Akbar’s narrow escapes and coronation on a dusty platform far from any city.

i18n.hi: उसने तक़दीर के झूले को झूलते देखा—हुमायूँ की वापसी, दिल्ली की लाइब्रेरी की सीढ़ियों से उसका गिरना, नन्हे अकबर की बाल-बाल बचतें और किसी शहर से दूर धूल भरे चबूतरे पर उसका ताजपोशी।

panels.shot: medium shot, intimate interior of Akbar’s courtly audience with women, side angle
panels.action: In a refined women’s audience chamber at Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar, glimpsed through a screen, leans forward in respectful conversation with Gulbadan, who sits on a raised cushion, her posture calm, attendants around them.

dialogue.text: Under Akbar, Gulbadan became more than a shadow of the past. As senior aunt she advised, negotiated marriages, and represented a living bridge to Babur and Humayun in a court hungry for its own origin story.

i18n.hi: अकबर के राज में गुलबदन सिर्फ़ अतीत की परछाईं नहीं रहीं। सीनियर फूफी के तौर पर वो सलाह देती, शादियाँ तय करातीं और बाबर-हुमायूँ से जोड़ी हुई ज़िंदा कड़ी बनकर उस दरबार को उसकी जड़ें दिखातीं जो अपनी कहानी का भूखा था।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Gulbadan presenting a petition-like scroll, three-quarter view
panels.action: In another scene within Akbar’s palace, Gulbadan, dignified, holds a folded scroll before her chest, her eyes intent, as Akbar’s figure listens from behind a perforated screen, underscoring her access and authority.

dialogue.text: When she and other royal women sought permission for the Hajj, their voices carried weight. Through petitions and quiet insistence, they argued for a journey many deemed too perilous for the haram.

i18n.hi: जब उसने और दूसरी शाही औरतों ने हज की इजाज़त माँगी, उनकी आवाज़ हल्की नहीं थी। अरज़दारियों और चुप मगर सख़्त ज़िद से उन्होंने उस सफ़र का हक़ माँगा जिसे कई लोग हरम के लिए हद से ज़्यादा ख़तरनाक कहते थे।

panels.shot: epic wide shot of caravan on the move, slightly low angle
panels.action: A vast caravan stretches across the Rann-like landscape: camels laden with chests, litters carrying veiled women, soldiers riding ahead; at the centre, Gulbadan’s curtained howdah moves with measured grace, the sea hinted far beyond.

dialogue.text: In 1575, Gulbadan led an imperial caravan towards the sea, bound for the Hajj. For seven years she and other women of the dynasty traveled, prayed and negotiated the long route between Hindustan and the Holy Cities.

i18n.hi: 1575 में गुलबदन ने शाही क़ाफ़िला समंदर की ओर हज के लिए रवाना किया। सात बरस तक वो और सल्तनत की और औरतें चलती रहीं, इबादत करती रहीं और हिन्दुस्तान से पवित्र शहरों तक हर मोड़ पर सौदे और समझौते करती रहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a coastal port, bird’s-eye angle
panels.action: At a bustling Indian port, ships with billowing lateen sails are moored; Gulbadan’s party of women, guards and porters winds along the pier toward a ship’s gangplank, the wind whipping veils and banners.

dialogue.text: They crossed seas from an Indian port toward Arabia, part pilgrims, part diplomats, their presence weaving Mughal authority into the wider currents of Indian Ocean trade, Ottoman power and sacred travel.

i18n.hi: वे हिन्दुस्तानी बन्दरगाह से अरब की तरफ़ समंदर पार गए—आधा मुसाफ़िर, आधा एलची—अपनी मौजूदगी से मुग़ल असर को हिन्द महासागर की गिरोह में, उस्मानी ताक़त में और मुक़द्दस सफ़रों की राहों में पिरोते हुए।

panels.shot: medium wide shot of a camp near the Haramain, twilight
panels.action: A modest camp stands under a desert sky; Gulbadan sits outside a tent, hands raised in prayer, while women move quietly behind her and distant city lights suggest Mecca or Medina beyond the dunes.

dialogue.text: In and around the Holy Places, Gulbadan’s life braided devotion with politics: receiving envoys, managing finances, responding to news from Akbar’s court, and preserving the dignity of Mughal women far from home.

i18n.hi: पवित्र जगहों में और उनके आस-पास गुलबदन की ज़िंदगी में इबादत और सियासत घुल-मिल गई—वो रुके हुए एलचियों को मिलती, हिसाब-किताब सँभालती, अकबर के दरबार से आती खबरों पर जवाब भेजती और घर से दूर रहते हुए भी मुग़ल बेगमों की इज़्ज़त बचाए रखती।

panels.shot: medium shot on ship’s deck, horizon level
panels.action: On the deck of a returning ship, Gulbadan sits under a canopy, holding onto a rope rail as waves rise; a younger attendant points excitedly toward the faint line of the Indian coast reappearing.

dialogue.text: By the early 1580s she returned, seasoned by years of movement, storms and negotiations. The journey itself would leave only scattered traces, but it had sharpened her eye for how fragile power and safety could be.

i18n.hi: 1580 के शुरू में वो लौटी—सालों के सफ़र, तूफ़ानों और बातचीतों से तपकर। इस सफ़र के चिह्न तो इतिहास में बिखरे रह गए, पर इसने उसकी नज़र को सत्ता और अमन की नाज़ुकी पर और तेज़ कर दिया।

panels.shot: medium interior shot, low angle behind her shoulder, focusing on page
panels.action: Back in Fatehpur Sikri, Gulbadan sits before her writing desk, a clean sheet laid out; from over her shoulder we see the first curling Persian lines forming, careful yet firm, as a lamp burns beside the page.

dialogue.text: When Akbar called for histories of his house, Gulbadan answered not as an ornament but as an author. She set herself to write the Humayun-Nama, a woman’s view onto the storms of a man’s reign.

i18n.hi: जब अकबर ने अपने ख़ानदान की तवारीख़ माँगी, गुलबदन ने ज़ेवर की तरह नहीं, लेखक की तरह जवाब दिया। उसने हुमायूँनामा लिखने का बीड़ा उठाया—एक औरत की नज़र से मर्द के तख़्त की आंधियाँ।

panels.shot: tight shot on her hand and pen, extreme close-up
panels.action: Her ink-stained fingers hold a reed pen above the manuscript, mid-stroke; the texture of the paper and the blackness of fresh ink stand out, the script clear yet stylized, the scene intimate and focused.

dialogue.text: She wrote in Persian of quarrels in the haram, of brothers’ divisions, of everyday routines and sudden disasters, anchoring grand events in small, observed moments rather than in the flattery expected of courtly chronicles.

i18n.hi: उसने फ़ारसी में हरम के झगड़ों, भाइयों के फूट, रोज़मर्रा की दिनचर्या और अचानक टूट पड़ने वाली आफ़तों को लिखा—बड़े वाकियात को उन छोटे, देखे हुए पलों में बाँधते हुए, जहाँ दरबारी तारीख़ों वाली चापलूसी की जगह नहीं थी।

panels.shot: medium shot, two female attendants nearby, side angle
panels.action: As Gulbadan dictates a passage to a young woman who copies on another sheet, a second attendant grinds ink at a low table; Gulbadan’s mouth is slightly open mid-sentence, her expression intent and controlled.

dialogue.text: Sometimes she wrote with her own hand, sometimes she dictated. In either case, the choices of what to tell and how to tell it were hers, shaped by loyalty to Humayun and by a clear memory of his failings.

i18n.hi: कभी वो खुद लिखती, कभी बोलकर लिखवाती। दोनों ही हाल में क्या कहना है, कैसे कहना है, ये चुनाव उसी का था—जो हुमायूँ से वफ़ादारी और उसकी कमज़ोरियों की साफ़ याद दोनों से आकार लेता था।

panels.shot: memory montage, soft focus, medium-wide interior
panels.action: Within a blurred overlay of scenes—Humayun consulting astrologers, women packing hurriedly for flight, a quiet reconciliation—Gulbadan sits steady in the foreground, writing, her calm demeanour contrasting with the turbulence of the images behind.

dialogue.text: Her narrative did not stride like an official victory scroll. It moved between private rooms and public decisions, between letters and journeys, letting readers feel how imperial choices rippled through the lives of wives, sisters and daughters.

i18n.hi: उसकी कहानी कोई सरकारी फ़तहनामा की तरह सीधी march नहीं करती। वो निजी कमरों और सार्वजनिक फ़ैसलों के बीच, ख़तों और सफ़रों के बीच घूमती है, ताकि पाठक महसूस करें कि बादशाहों के फ़ैसले बीवियों, बहनों और बेटियों की ज़िंदगी में कैसे लहर बनकर घुसते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot, contemplative, window light on her face
panels.action: Gulbadan pauses in her writing, looking up toward a shaft of light, her pen resting on the page, as if weighing a memory before choosing whether to set it down or leave it in silence.

dialogue.text: She wrote within the bounds of family loyalty, sometimes veiling conflict, sometimes hinting at it. Even in what she left unsaid, her careful omissions reveal how a woman at court navigated truth, discretion and authority.

i18n.hi: उसने ख़ानदान की वफ़ादारी की हदों के भीतर लिखा—कहीं टकराव को ढका, कहीं बस इशारा किया। जो कुछ उसने नहीं कहा, वो भी दिखा देता है कि दरबार की औरत सच, राज़दारी और अपने असर के बीच कैसे राह निकालती थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of an imperial library room, slightly high angle
panels.action: In an imperial library, clerks and calligraphers move among volumes; Gulbadan’s completed folios rest on a low stand, while a librarian gently lifts one, its margins decorated sparsely, the script neat, the air reverent.

dialogue.text: Her work joined the growing pile of histories ordered by Akbar, but it was unlike the others—a first-person record by a Mughal woman, preserving not only battles and treaties but the textures of a shared household past.

i18n.hi: उसकी किताब अकबर के हुक्म पर लिखी जा रही तवारीख़ के ढेर में जा लगी, पर वो उन सबसे अलग थी—एक मुग़ल औरत की पहली शख़्सी गवाही, जिसमें जंगों और मुआहिदों के साथ-साथ साझा घर की रोज़मर्रा की बनावट भी महफ़ूज़ हो गई।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot of a single manuscript on a table, lamp-lit, overhead angle
panels.action: A lone manuscript volume lies open on a wooden stand in a dim chamber, a lamp shining onto its Persian lines; beyond, darkness suggests shelves of other lost or hidden texts, the single book fragile yet luminous.

dialogue.text: Only one incomplete manuscript of her Humayun-Nama survives, carried far from the court to a distant library. Yet in those surviving pages, Gulbadan Begum’s voice still widens our understanding of empire, family and who may write history.

i18n.hi: उसके हुमायूँनामा का सिर्फ़ एक अधूरा नुस्ख़ा बचा है, जो दरबार से दूर किसी अजनबी कुतुबख़ाने तक जा पहुँचा। फिर भी उन बचे पन्नों में गुलबदन बेगम की आवाज़ आज भी हमारे लिए साम्राज्य, ख़ानदान और 'इतिहास लिखने का हक़ किसका है'—इन सब की हदें फैलाए रखती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Gulbadan Begum and the Memory of an Empire
subtitle_i18n.hi: गुलबदन बेगम और एक साम्राज्य की याद
